header: THE BREAKING-NEWS WATCH. A tab is kept fresh for 30 minutes (5 while it holds a priority story), which is right for the ordinary run of news and would be too slow for the news that matters: a death, a big accident, a diplomatic visit. So every three minutes, when somebody is looking, the route reads a few of the quickest feeds of each language and tests their headlines with the priority rules (priority.ts). The first reading only notes what is there; after that, a priority headline that was not there before makes the three language tabs OLD at once, so that the next asking is answered from what is kept while a new tab is made in the background, and the story is on the screen within the next minute's check. The 30 minutes are broken for that news only. (A headline that the tab will then leave out, for having no picture or being paid, costs one extra rebuild, nothing more.)
